findings.claim: releaseHalfOpenProbe releases a probe slot whenever a success or failure is recorded during HALF_OPEN, even if the underlying request never took a slot, such as a request admitted while CLOSED or a probe from an earlier HALF_OPEN window whose counter was reset to 0 by transitionToOpen or transitionToHalfOpen. As a result more requests than the intended cap (e.g. 3 when threshold is 10 and rate is 30) can reach the upstream simultaneously, making the cap effectively soft rather than a hard limit, though it remains bounded because late failures still count toward re-opening.

canProceed now reserves a slot by incrementing halfOpenInFlight, but its name and JSDoc still describe it as a read-only check; a caller that only calls it to check status without later calling recordSuccess or recordFailure will hold a slot forever, and once enough slots are held this way every request gets blocked until stale-circuit cleanup removes the circuit after 10x rollingWindow.

The JSDoc for canProceed (returns false if circuit is open) and canProceedOrFail (throws if circuit is open) is out of date because it does not mention that a true/non-throwing result in HALF_OPEN also reserves a probe slot that must be released via record*, and does not cover the case where the circuit is full in HALF_OPEN.
getOrRegisterCircuit is changed to private as part of an unrelated refactor bundled into this PR rather than a separate change scoped to the probe cap fix, making the diff harder to review.
recordFailure now registers circuits itself, a behavioral change unrelated to the probe cap fix that is bundled into the same PR rather than split out or called out explicitly in the PR description.
recordSuccess now checks the enabled flag, another change unrelated to the probe cap fix bundled into this PR, increasing the size and review difficulty of the diff.

The getOrRegisterCircuit call is removed from network.module.ts as part of the bundled registration refactor, which is a separate concern from the probe cap change and should be split into its own PR or explicitly named in the PR body.

The new recordSuccess test uses the literal circuit name 'new-circuit' instead of the faker-generated circuitName used elsewhere in the file, making the test suite inconsistent with the stated convention of using faker values instead of literals.

The edited 'circuit-1' and 'circuit-2' tests kept their literal circuit name strings instead of being updated to use faker-generated values, leaving the spec file inconsistent since the rest of the file was moved to faker-generated circuitName.

There is no test through the network wrapper verifying the probe cap end-to-end, even though releasing a slot depends on the wrapper calling record* on every completion path; for example a 4xx response calls recordSuccess while a blocked request throws before the try block and so records nothing, and network.module.integration.spec.ts has no HALF_OPEN case covering this.

The ARCHITECTURE doc gives the probe cap formula as threshold x halfOpenFailureRateThreshold / 100 without noting that the code rounds up with Math.ceil (circuit-breaker.service.ts:351), so the documented formula does not match the implementation's rounding behavior.
